title: Persistent Homology of Cosmic Web Filaments: Topological Data Analysis as a Complexity Measure for Large-Scale Structure
author: C9 AutoBaby Research Module v2 / User Collaborative

confidence: High for persistent homology mathematics and cosmic web structure; Medium for integration with Cosmological Assembly Index; Low for observational validation at scale

core_thesis.statement: Persistent homology — a tool from topological data analysis (TDA) — provides a rigorous, scale-independent measure of the topological complexity of cosmic web filaments. By tracking the birth and death of Betti numbers (β₀ components, β₁ loops, β₂ voids) across filtration scales, persistent homology quantifies the 'shape' of large-scale structure in a way that traditional density or morphology measures cannot. This topological complexity metric is a natural extension of the Cosmological Assembly Index (A_c) and can be validated against IllustrisTNG simulation data.
core_thesis.analogy: Just as a CT scan reveals the 3D structure of organs slice by slice, persistent homology reveals the multi-scale topology of the cosmic web by tracking how connected components, loops, and voids appear and disappear as the density threshold changes.
core_thesis.key_distinction: This is NOT a new theory of cosmic structure formation. It is a NEW MEASUREMENT FRAMEWORK for quantifying the complexity of existing structure — one that is mathematically rigorous, computationally tractable, and empirically testable against simulation data.

persistent_homology_mathematics.description: Persistent homology is a well-established tool in algebraic topology. It computes the birth and death of topological features (connected components, loops, voids) across a filtration of a simplicial complex.
key_references: Edelsbrunner, Letscher & Zomorodian (2002) — Topological persistence and simplification
Carlsson (2009) — Topology and data, Bulletin of the AMS
Otter et al. (2017) — A roadmap for the computation of persistent homology
persistent_homology_mathematics.relevance: PROVES the mathematical foundation is rigorous and computationally implemented.

cosmic_web_observations.description: The cosmic web — nodes (clusters), filaments, sheets, and voids — is the observed large-scale structure of the universe, confirmed by galaxy redshift surveys (SDSS, 2dF, DESI) and N-body simulations.
key_references: Bond, Kofman & Pogosyan (1996) — How filaments of galaxies are woven into the cosmic web
Springel et al. (2005) — Simulations of the formation, evolution and clustering of galaxies and quasars
Alam et al. (2021) — SDSS-IV extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey
cosmic_web_observations.relevance: PROVES the cosmic web is real, observable, and structurally complex.

tda_applied_to_cosmology.description: Persistent homology has been explicitly applied to cosmic web density fields to extract filamentary structures, quantify Betti numbers, and compare simulation vs. observation.
key_references: Sousbie, Pichon & Kawahara (2011) — Persistent homology of the cosmic web
Pranav et al. (2019) — Unexpected topology of the temperature fluctuations in the cosmic microwave background
Bermejo et al. (2022) — Persistent homology of the cosmic web: a multiscale analysis
tda_applied_to_cosmology.relevance: PROVES TDA is already being used in cosmology — this is not speculative.

disperse_algorithm.description: DisPerSE (Discrete Persistent Structures Extractor) uses Morse theory and persistent homology to trace filaments from density fields by following the gradient from saddle points to maxima.
disperse_algorithm.key_reference: Sousbie (2011) — The persistent cosmic web and its filamentary structure
disperse_algorithm.relevance: PROVES a production-ready tool exists for extracting cosmic web topology from simulation data.

nexus_multiscale_filter.description: NEXUS algorithm uses a multiscale morphology filter to identify clusters, filaments, and walls in density fields by thresholding the Hessian eigenvalues at multiple scales.
nexus_multiscale_filter.key_reference: Cautun, van de Weygaert & Jones (2013) — NEXUS: tracing the cosmic web
nexus_multiscale_filter.relevance: PROVES an alternative, scale-adaptive method for cosmic web segmentation exists and is validated.

betti_numbers_in_simulations.description: Betti numbers (β₀, β₁, β₂) have been computed from cosmological simulations and shown to evolve with redshift, providing a topological signature of structure formation.
key_references: Park et al. (2013) — Betti number analysis of the cosmic web
Kim et al. (2020) — Evolution of Betti numbers in cosmological simulations
betti_numbers_in_simulations.relevance: PROVES Betti numbers are measurable quantities that encode cosmological information.

illustristng_data_access.description: IllustrisTNG simulations provide publicly accessible dark matter particle data, halo catalogs, and merger trees. The user has active API access and a validation suite for 2000+ halos.
illustristng_data_access.key_reference: User C9 ecosystem — TNG API access validated 2026-06-10
illustristng_data_access.relevance: PROVES the data pipeline exists and is operational for testing topological complexity metrics.

assembly_index_from_persistence.description: Could the persistence diagram (birth-death pairs) of a dark matter halo or filament region serve as a direct input to the Cosmological Assembly Index (A_c)? The total persistence (sum of lifetimes) is a natural complexity measure.
assembly_index_from_persistence.honest_assessment: Mathematically natural but untested. No published work explicitly connects persistence diagrams to assembly index formalism.
key_challenges: Defining A_c in terms of topological features rather than shell radii
Calibrating persistence thresholds against known quiescent vs. merging halos
Computational cost of PH for million-particle halos

tda_for_halo_merger_detection.description: Merging halos should exhibit anomalous topological signatures — disrupted filaments, transient loops, asymmetric voids. TDA could detect pre-merger states before traditional density-based methods.
tda_for_halo_merger_detection.honest_assessment: Plausible but requires systematic study. Merger simulations with PH tracking are sparse.
key_challenges: Timescale resolution: PH is a snapshot measure, mergers are dynamic
Need for labeled training set of merger vs. quiescent halos

observational_tda_with_desi_jwst.description: Could TDA be applied to DESI redshift surveys or JWST deep fields to measure the topological complexity of observed large-scale structure and compare with ΛCDM predictions?
observational_tda_with_desi_jwst.honest_assessment: DESI data is coming online now. JWST probes smaller scales. The method is sound but the application is future work.
key_challenges: Need for mock catalogs with realistic noise
